## Overview

This vignette demonstrates the application of OmniCorr to cattle
host–microbiome multi-omics data.

The analysis integrates six proteomics layers:

- Archaeal and bacterial proteomics (reference layer)
- Ciliate proteomics
- Fungal proteomics
- Metazoan proteomics from rumen digesta
- Host liver proteomics
- Host rumen wall proteomics

This vignette uses precomputed WGCNA module eigengenes to demonstrate the
integration of microbial and host proteomics data using OmniCorr.
Details about data processing and sample alignment are provided in the
Data provenance section.

## Data provenance

The module eigengenes used in this vignette were generated from the
original cattle multi-omics datasets using the WGCNA workflow provided
in `Case_Study_2/Cattle_OmniCorr/Rumen_OmniCorr.Rmd`.

WGCNA was performed separately for each omics layer. The resulting
module eigengenes were aligned using sample identifiers, retaining
the 20 samples shared across all six omics layers.

The processed eigengenes are distributed with OmniCorr as
`cattle_module_eigengenes.rds` to make this vignette reproducible
without rerunning the computationally intensive WGCNA analysis.

The original WGCNA workflow is retained in the project repository
for reference and reproducibility.

## Load the data

```{r load-data}
library(OmniCorr)

cattle_file <- system.file(
  "extdata",
  "cattle_module_eigengenes.rds",
  package = "OmniCorr",
  mustWork = TRUE
)

cattle_MEs <- readRDS(cattle_file)

sapply(cattle_MEs, dim)
```

## Calculate correlations

We first calculate correlations between the archaeal/bacterial
module eigengenes and the rumen digesta metazoan module eigengenes.

```{r correlations}
cor_results <- calculate_correlations(
  df1 = cattle_MEs$Archbac,
  df2 = cattle_MEs$Metazoa,
  method = "pearson",
  show_significance = "stars"
)

head(cor_results$correlation)
```

## Integrate multiple omics layers

We use the archaeal/bacterial proteomics modules as the central
reference layer and compare them with the other five layers.

```{r omnicorr-heatmap, fig.width=11, fig.height=8}
comparison_layers <- cattle_MEs[
  c("Ciliates", "Fungi", "Metazoa", "Liver", "Wall")
]

omnicorr_plot <- run_omnicorr(
  reference_layer = cattle_MEs$Archbac,
  comparison_layers = comparison_layers
)

ComplexHeatmap::draw(omnicorr_plot)
```

## Interpretation

The resulting heatmap visualizes correlations between
archaeal/bacterial proteomics modules and modules from microbial
and host proteomics layers.

Positive and negative correlations indicate associations between
module eigengenes. These relationships may suggest coordinated
biological processes but do not establish direct interactions
or causality.
